findings.message: Under 071 a PM can see someone's hours only for the weeks that hold hours on a project the PM approves (`hoursVisibleTo`). `loadInputs` still counts that person as soon as any hours are visible (`hours.has(p.userId)`). Their available hours cover the whole month, but logged and billable hours come only from the visible weeks. The hidden weeks therefore count as zero hours, and the report shows a lower utilisation as if it were that person's real figure. It also lowers the team figure. Fix: when the viewer can see only some of a person's weeks in the range, mark the row as partial or not visible (as the leave case does with 'Leave not visible to you') and leave it out of the team figure. Or limit the PM's view to people whose whole range they can see.
findings.scenario: Nimal is PM of Fleet Tracker. In October, Kasun logs 40 h on Fleet Tracker in W42 and 120 h on Contoso Portal in W41, W43 and W44, all billable, with 176 h available. Nimal's get_utilisation shows Kasun at about 23% (40/176) instead of about 91%, and the team figure goes down with it.

findings.message: 071 limits every Admin act on other people's time to the owner's legal entity (`adminOver`, `inEntity`). `setSettings` checks only `action: "time:admin"`. `can()` with no `legalEntityId` ignores `legalEntityIds`, so an Admin scoped to one entity can still change the tenant's entry rules. Those rules then refuse logs for people in every other entity. Fix: refuse the write unless the caller holds `time:admin` on an assignment with no entity scope (`legalEntityIds === null`). Do the same in `proposeSettings` so no chat card is shown, and add a test with an entity-scoped Admin.
findings.scenario: An Admin whose role assignment covers only the AU entity calls set_time_settings { backdateWeeks: 1, allowFuture: false }. The change succeeds, and an LK engineer's log_time for a day two weeks back is then refused with 'time can be logged up to 1 week back'.

findings.message: 071 narrows who reviews a request by the owner's legal entity only in `reviews()`. `scopeSql` stays the wider pre-071 rule (comment at line 63). `get_change_requests` takes `PAGE` rows by that wider SQL scope and filters them after the limit, so it no longer pages in SQL by the real scope (the 070 fix). For an entity-scoped approver, `can(v,'time:approve')` without an entity is true, so the SQL fetches every request in the tenant, and a page can be empty or short while `truncated` is true. Fix: put the owner's entity into `scopeSql` (join `auth.user` and filter on `legal_entity_id` against the viewer's assignments for `time:approve`) so the SQL and `chainFor` stay the same rule.
findings.scenario: An Admin scoped to LK, in a tenant where the 60 newest change requests belong to AU people. get_change_requests returns {requests: [], truncated: true, before: …}. An agent reports 'no change requests' even though LK requests exist on the next page.

findings.message: `reaches` is exported but never used. It also repeats the entity-reach test inlined in `approvesIn`, so the two copies can drift apart. Remove it, or have `approvesIn` use it.

`logOnce` checks for a replay outside the `logTime` service, in its own read. So when a replay matches, `log_time` returns a value without reaching its declared service at all. Chat counts writes on confirm, and `packages/chat/src/engine.ts:304-305` closes an ok run with `writes === 0` as unknown ("couldn't confirm what it changed"). The `log_time` input schema offers `clientRef` to chat as well, so a confirmed card whose ref is already logged reads as unknown, not done. The `source_taken` fallback path does reach the service once, so the two replay paths end differently. Fix: do the lookup inside `logTime`'s `run`, in its transaction, and return the existing entry as the service result (one keyed call). Or keep `clientRef` out of the chat path.
findings.scenario: An agent's chat turn proposes log_time {FLT, 2026-10-27, 2h, clientRef:'run-41'} after the same clientRef was already logged over MCP. Confirming the card shows 'couldn't confirm what it changed', yet the entry exists and nothing was written.

findings.message: The Reports README says a PM sees 'people with hours on a project they manage in the month'. The code (`hoursVisibleTo`) and the Time README decide week by week: a PM sees only the weeks that hold hours on their project. Make the Reports README say per week.

`guardOwnDate` blocks the owner's own correct/delete outside the back-dating window. `requestChange` refuses rejected weeks ('fix it yourself'). Together, an approver's rejection of a week older than `backdateWeeks` leaves the owner no path of their own: correcting is refused as too early and requesting is refused as not locked. Only a PM or Admin fix gets it out. Consider exempting rejected weeks from the date window, or saying so in the reject flow.
findings.scenario: backdateWeeks=4. A PM rejects the owner's W38 week in W43. The owner's correct_time_entry is refused as 'too early', and request_time_change is refused with 'you can fix it yourself'.
